findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category (or uncategorized_category_id) row is absent
findings.body: The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking that any row came back. Site settings only get a row in `site_settings` when they differ from the default, so on most installs, including every fresh install, `embed_category` has no row. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the migration. Line 15 has the same problem for `uncategorized_category_id`. Check `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples` before indexing.

findings.title: Legacy host values inserted raw: unescaped and not normalized
findings.body:
Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into SQL as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote breaks the migration; the value should be passed through `quote`/`PG::Connection.escape_string`.

The values are also never normalized. The old setting accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, and old code stripped the scheme at lookup time. The migration skips the model's `before_validation` stripping, so those rows keep the scheme/path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match, and existing embeds stop working after upgrade.

Trailing `\r`/whitespace and blank lines are not stripped either.

findings.title: Hosts with a port can never match; lookup isn't truly case-insensitive
findings.body:
The validation explicitly allows a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and `before_validation` keeps it. `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so a saved host like `example.com:8080` can never be allowed.

Also, `lower(host) = ?` lowercases only the stored column, not the argument. Ruby's URI does not downcase the host, so a referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/...` is rejected. Downcase `host` before querying.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. That happens with `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or when the admin controller receives a request without `embeddable_host[:host]`. The result is a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?`.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 for unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil. `host.destroy` and `save_host(host)` then raise NoMethodError instead of returning 404. Use `find` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: Embedded `_ids` hydration crashes on null and keeps unresolved entries
findings.body: `obj[k].map` throws if a serialized `*_ids` key is null or not an array. `hydrated || []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array. Ids that cannot be resolved become `undefined` entries in the array instead of being filtered out.

findings.title: type.replace only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with more than one underscore will not be recognized and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use a global regex such as `/_/g`.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches behavior
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts. This test, "is false if embeddable_host is blank", now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false, so it does not test what its name claims. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested before block is likewise irrelevant to the outcome.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators. It works because all fabricators get loaded, but it is clearly a mistake and will confuse anyone looking for the category fabricator.
